subject: Private VPC: control-plane delegation & data egress review
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@stratusops.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private VPC: control-plane delegation & data egress review

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, attached is a first-pass segmentation diagram (segmentation_diagram_v1.pdf) and a short policy matrix (network_policy_matrix.xlsx) that outline:
- control-plane connectivity options (managed control plane vs. delegated control plane inside customer VPC)
- data-plane egress paths and recommended egress-proxy pattern
- minimal firewall rules for canary workloads

Could you PTAL and confirm the following so we can finalize the reference:
1) Do you want the control plane endpoints to be reachable over VPC peering, or do you prefer a private VNet endpoint with strict CIDR allowlist?
2) Does StratusOps have a preferred egress inspection appliance (Palo Alto / Zscaler / in-house) we should route through?
3) Any blackout windows for config changes next week?

If it helps, Markus and I can run a short architecture review with your network team on Thursday (30 minutes). Proposed agenda: architecture walk, threat surface, runbook handoff items.

Thanks — looking forward to locking the design down.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: segmentation_diagram_v1.pdf (diagram, 1 page); network_policy_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@stratusops.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: StratusOps Network Team <net@stratusops.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC: control-plane delegation & data egress review

Grace —

Thanks for the notes and artifacts. Quick answers inline:  
1) Prefer private endpoint with allowlist — we want outbound-only from our VPC to the control plane where possible, so a VNet endpoint with CIDR restrictions is our preference.
2) We run an on-prem ZTNA appliance currently (in-house) that terminates egress inspection; we'd prefer routing through that so we can apply existing DLP/inspection.
3) No scheduled blackouts next week.

A few clarifying questions from the network team:
- If we push the control-plane proxy inside our VPC, what auth model does Redwood expect for Webhook callbacks (mTLS, short-lived certs, token)?
- How will KV cache and training artifact uploads be routed; do you expect any wide-open ports?

Happy to join the Thursday review.

—Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Infrastructure, StratusOps
sanjay.patel@stratusops.com

Date: 2026-10-20T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC: control-plane delegation & data egress review

Sanjay —

Good questions. High level answers:
- We recommend short-lived client certs (mutual TLS) between the customer-side control-plane proxy and Redwood for webhook callbacks; tokens alone increase the blast radius. We can support both, but mTLS is the default for delegated control-plane flows.
- KV cache and artifacts: all uploads should be outbound to a pre-signed S3 endpoint (or equivalent). No inbound ACLs necessary except for a tightly-scoped control-plane callback port (mTLS).

I'll add the mTLS detail to the diagram and matrix and loop our infra engineer (PrIyom) to validate tunnel/peering considerations.

Thanks,
Grace

From: PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@stratusops.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Private VPC: control-plane delegation & data egress review

Thanks for the context — I reviewed the v1 diagram. A few internal notes before the 30-minute review:
- We'll propose a delegated control-plane proxy deployed as a customer-managed service in their VPC (k8s DaemonSet or small autoscaling group) that terminates mTLS to Redwood and exposes a local metrics/health port to customer monitoring.
- Egress: route artifact uploads out to a pre-signed S3 gateway (TLS) via the customer's inspection appliance. No inbound NAT required.
- If StratusOps wants VPC peering, we should avoid asymmetric routing by ensuring the tunnel/peering is used only for control plane signaling; data-plane artifacts use direct internet egress (to preserve throughput control).

Attaching a tightened diagram (segmentation_diagram_v2.pdf) with the mTLS/TLS annotations and a short runbook stub (private-vpc-handoff-runbook.md). Please review before the walkthrough; I'll highlight the diff in the review.

- PrIyom

Attachments: segmentation_diagram_v2.pdf; private-vpc-handoff-runbook.md

From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@stratusops.com>

Cc: StratusOps Network Team <net@stratusops.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC: control-plane delegation & data egress review

PrIyom / Grace —

Thanks for the tightened diagram. Couple of notes from our side after an internal sync:
- mTLS for callbacks is acceptable; we will create a CSR workflow for short-lived certs and share the trust bundle.
- We prefer artifact uploads to go via a dedicated NAT gateway and then through our inspection appliance (to preserve audit logs). Can you confirm there are no special source-IP dependencies on Redwood's side (we will be NAT-ing to a small pool of egress IPs)?
- We also want a short checklist for rollback in case the delegated proxy fails (how traffic will fallback to Redwood-hosted endpoints).

If you can confirm the source-IP behavior and add a brief rollback checklist to the runbook, we can approve and schedule an ops handoff.

—Sanjay

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@stratusops.com>, PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-23T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC: control-plane delegation & data egress review — confirmed next steps

Great — thanks for the signoff items. Quick confirmations and next steps: 
- Source IP: Redwood will accept connections from the NAT egress pool; we do not require fixed source IPs for artifact ingestion (pre-signed URLs keep the upload secure). However, for control-plane callbacks (mTLS), we will register the trust bundle with the specific proxy identity — no source IP whitelist required.
- Rollback checklist: we'll add a short rollback path to the runbook: 1) flip DNS to Redwood-hosted control-plane endpoint, 2) scale up ephemeral fallback pool (we automate this via the rollout policy), 3) notify on-call and revert cert rotations if needed. Added to private-vpc-handoff-runbook.md.

Action items:
- PrIyom: finalize runbook checklist + push final segmentation_diagram_v2.pdf to the shared Drive (target: end of day Friday).
- Neha: open internal ticket for a scoped egress IP pool mapping with our infra team.
- Grace/Markus: schedule the 30-minute ops handoff with StratusOps for next Tuesday.

Thanks everyone — I'll update the HubSpot deal and attach the final artifacts.

Best,
Grace

Attachments referenced: segmentation_diagram_v2.pdf; private-vpc-handoff-runbook.md
